subject: Life Skills
title: Groupthink
description: A micro-lesson that makes Groupthink usable.

hook.text: NASA launched Challenger despite engineer warnings. The team wanted consensus so badly they ignored the dissent.

buildup.text: Irving Janis coined 'groupthink' in 1972. It happens when cohesion becomes more important than critical evaluation.

discovery.text: Signs: self-censorship, illusion of unanimity, pressure on dissenters, and collective rationalization of bad ideas.

twist.text: Groupthink is most dangerous in smart teams. High confidence plus social pressure kills the habit of questioning.

climax.text: Assign a devil's advocate in every important meeting. Make disagreement a job, not a personality risk.

punchline.text: Harmony that silences doubt is not harmony. It is danger.

quiz.question: What is the best structural defense against groupthink?
options: Assigning someone the role of devil's advocate
